content:
Priya: FYI — AcmeCorp escalated: several Console dashboards returning empty frames + intermittent 500s from analytics API since ~09:40 PST. They see long spinner then a 500. Dash IDs: 91c3, 91c4, 91d0.
Ethan: Are they on Hosted or Dedicated? Can you grab a request id from the browser network tab and a full panel request payload?
Priya: Hosted (prod). Got a req id from their browser network: req=abcd-1234-xy. Time window ~2024-06-18T09:38:00-09:52:00 PST. Pasting a sample curl/response we captured:
```
curl 'https://api.redwood-inference.com/analytics/query' -H 'authorization: Bearer xxxxxx' -d '{"dashboard_id":"91c3","panel_id":"p7","from":"2024-06-18T09:30:00Z","to":"2024-06-18T09:50:00Z"}'
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
{"error":"analytics aggregator: upstream query failed","request_id":"abcd-1234-xy"}
```
Jordan: I'm seeing a correlated spike on analytics-aggregator around that window: CPU and query queue depth shot up. ClickHouse also returned slow query errors. Looks like a heavy GROUP BY across high-cardinality tags.
Priya: Log excerpt for req abcd-1234-xy: 
```
[2024-06-18T09:41:12Z] req=abcd-1234-xy level=error module=analytics-agg msg="QueryExecutionTimeout: query exceeded 30s" query_id=qh-77a
[2024-06-18T09:41:12Z] req=abcd-1234-xy level=warn module=proxy msg="fallthrough, returning 500 to client"
```
AcmeCorp Support: This started after they refreshed a big dashboard, affects multiple users. Dashboards intermittently load if you retry but usually spinner/500.
Ethan: Possible culprits: sudden high-cardinality filter, retention/rollup mismatch, or cache eviction. Can you repro by running the underlying query directly against ClickHouse with the same time range and group keys? Also check if the prefix cache was evicted at 09:40.
Jordan: Quick repro I ran (sanitized) to show heavy ops: 
```sql
SELECT customer_id, metric, toStartOfMinute(ts) as t, sum(value)
FROM metrics.events
WHERE ts BETWEEN toDateTime('2024-06-18 09:30:00') AND toDateTime('2024-06-18 09:50:00')
AND org = 'acme-acct'
GROUP BY customer_id, metric, t
ORDER BY t
```
This produces a lot of groups for that org for this window — ClickHouse work_mem spikes and query takes > 40s.
Priya: Customer confirmed they didn't change the dashboard but did onboard a new integration that increased cardinality at ~09:35.
Ethan: Short-term mitigation options: 1) ask customer to narrow time range or remove a high-cardinality series; 2) enable panel-level fallback (serve zeros) so dashboard UI loads; 3) adjust aggregator query timeout or add a retryable 502 so UI can surface 'partial results'.
Jordan: I pushed a temporary feature-flag that enables the panel fallback for acme-acct only. Path: https://console.redwood-inference.com/flags/analytics-panel-fallback -> toggled for org acme-acct. Steps I ran:
```bash
# enable fallback for org
http PATCH https://console.redwood-inference.com/api/flags/analytics-panel-fallback org=acme-acct enabled=true
```
DeployBot: rollouts-controller: flag update applied to acme-acct (env: prod) — rollout finished in 12s.
Priya: Confirmed with customer — dashboards now load (panels show faded "partial data" and zeros) so UX is unblocked. They're OK with this while we fix root cause.
Ethan: I'll open an infra ticket to: (a) inspect ClickHouse query plan for qh-77a, (b) add a LIMIT/guard for high-cardinality GROUP BYs, (c) revisit aggregator timeouts and retry semantics. I'll also check if our prefix cache eviction policy kicked in at 09:40.
Priya: Logged support ticket SUP-4820 and attached the logs and timestamps. Notifying CS to confirm SLA remediation.
Jordan: Next engineering steps: collect profiling trace for that query, add a targeted roll-forward to make aggregator return 502+Retry-After for transient overloads, and consider adding a cost-estimator on queries to preemptively short-circuit pathological ones.
Priya: Thanks team — I'll update Acme and keep this thread open until fixes land. :thumbsup:
